transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... things at the warehouse have gotten pretty bad. The routing system we use, it isn't just a regular computer to me anymore. I know it's been marking my moves. It sends these messages through the scanners to push me out, just because I'm one of the old hands there. That's... well, that's what brings me in today.
How long have you been feeling that the routing system is sending you these messages?

Well, it's been going on for a while now. I'd say... about a year and eight months. That's how long I've been dealing with it—the messages from the scanners, and the voices that come with it. It's just been a constant thing for me since then.

Aside from these experiences with the scanners and the voices, have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep up with your daily routine, such as taking care of your personal hygiene or keeping your home organized?

Well, yeah, things have definitely slipped. My wife... she actually tells me my face has just gone flat, like I don't show much of anything anymore. And I guess I hardly answer her when she talks to me. 

As for getting things done around the house, I just... most days I just sit at the kitchen table. I'll sit there staring at my coffee instead of starting anything that actually needs doing. I just don't seem to have it in me to get going.
Besides the voices you mentioned, have you ever seen things that other people don't seem to see?

No, I don't think I've ever seen anything that isn't there. It's just the voices. Like... even when I'm at home, sitting out in my garage with everything completely shut off, I hear the dispatch voices. They come through clear as day. They'll call out my operator number and tell me I'm dangerous, or... or they'll say security is coming to get me. But no, I haven't seen anything unusual. Just hearing them.
